correctness.rationale: Normalized influence plus a strict response factor below one half makes every update a convex combination with a positive self-coefficient. Strict positive feedback along directed paths lowers the old maximum and raises the old minimum within n-1 steps; continuity and compactness imply consensus. The diameter displacement is at most twice the maximal edge response, and vanishing response-to-gap ratio forces D(t+1)/D(t)->1. In the reciprocal two-agent subfamily the exact gap recurrence is transformed by y=d^(-alpha) and H(y)=exp(y)y^(-(1+1/alpha)); rigorous mean-value asymptotics give H(y(t+1))-H(y(t))->2alpha, hence the three-term logarithmic law, epsilon hitting-time constant, and analytic-order comparison. Verified exact-rational and floating-point tests supplement, but do not replace, proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2024 full text proves qualitative agreement and depicts the identical flat-bias example, without quantitative rates. The later generalized-bias theorem similarly proves agreement but no sharp inverse-gap correction or epsilon-time equivalent. A distinct multipolar bias model and earlier confirmation-bias polarization results do not imply the same claims. Actual published-index searches, comparable original full-text sections and accessible historical claims were compared by implications. Residual risk from broad nonlinear-iteration theory is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Specialist slow-iteration/regular-variation theory could imply the scalar three-term formula through a more general asymptotic theorem; the mathematical novelty of generic Laplace asymptotic tools is not claimed.
Additional nonlinear consensus results may be unindexed or phrased in different variables.
Only the abstract was reviewed for the 2018 social-bias study; no full-text noncoverage finding is asserted for that source.

value.rationale: The exact 2024 example was introduced to illustrate extremely slow practical consensus, but no time-to-accuracy result was given. The new exponential-in-inverse-tolerance law quantifies that gap, and the graph-wide obstruction shows why connectivity cannot restore exponential progress when all response derivatives vanish at agreement. The analytic comparison separates regularities producing geometric, polynomial and inverse-logarithmic convergence, a motivated structural rate classification rather than a routine tabulation.
